T1 then trained a fresh PPO candidate for the maintainer allocation: the current recipe exposed it only to target radii 0.14-0.20 m, with actual completed steps rounded to 120,832 and a late training-proxy plateau near 0.96-0.97. Training proxies do not establish development performance, and the terminal checkpoint was not privileged. The archived late-plateau candidate T1:checkpoint-115712 was measured by M4 on 160 episodes spanning the official radius and angle distribution and achieved 105/160 successes (65.625%). M6 independently verified the grouped analysis and reported full panel coverage of 6.165-19.820 cm and -178.895 to 179.975 degrees. In the required bands, inner 6.0-<14.0 cm had 42/93 successes (45.16%), 48/93 first reaches, 45 failures before any reach, and 6 failures after reach without a complete hold; outer 14.0-20.0 cm had 63/67 successes (94.03%), 63/67 first reaches, 4 failures before any reach, and no post-reach incomplete-hold failures. Angle-sector success ranged from 48.39% to 92.11%, so angular coverage remains a residual artifact-level contributor. Interpretation supported by these observations: inner-radius/branch coverage and reset escape are the first consequential learned-policy bottleneck for this tested candidate, while post-arrival regulation is largely adequate after successful outer-band approach. This is a bounded candidate conclusion, not a causal proof that radius exposure alone, branch choice alone, or the PPO method broadly is responsible; M3 remains limited to its deterministic probes, and no official success result exists.
request.decision_frontier: I1's resolved distinction was inner-radius/branch coverage versus uninterrupted hold regulation. The completed evidence supports the former as the first bottleneck for T1: inner success is roughly half outer success, and the dominant inner deficit is failure before reach, whereas outer reached episodes complete the hold. The residual consequential distinction is among insufficient inner-radius exposure, reset singularity escape sequencing, IK branch selection, and angle-dependent coverage; M6's aggregate diagnostics do not identify which of these causes the artifact difference. The next discriminating candidate comparison should preserve the task and evaluation semantics while explicitly changing and recording inner-radius/branch/escape exposure, then repeat full official-range hold-complete diagnostics. A result that raises inner pre-reach success without degrading outer hold success supports coverage/escape as the useful intervention; persistent post-reach interruptions would reopen stabilization or temporal-memory investigation; broadly weak improvement would redirect toward representation or optimization rather than nominal plant authority.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal is at least 196 successes in the protected 200-episode assessment, with every success requiring an uninterrupted 100-step (2 s) hold within 1 cm. I1 produced and measured the first learned candidate but did not approach certification: the best-known candidate reached 65.625% on a 160-episode full official-range development panel.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Closed inquiry I1 by E5 after the closure condition was met. The next goal review should compare the expected contribution of an intervention targeted at inner-radius exposure/reset escape/branch coverage against the 65.625% best-known baseline, while preserving the full 100-step hold diagnostics. Do not request official assessment yet: the only measured candidate is far below 98% and the dominant failure regime is identified but not improved.
request.next_question: Can an explicitly broadened official-radius training exposure with deliberate reset-escape and two-branch coverage improve the inner-radius/approach deficit while preserving the candidate's outer-radius uninterrupted-hold performance under the full official distribution?

request.closure_condition: Train one bounded candidate under the explicitly broadened official-radius, reset-escape, and two-branch coverage recipe using the maintainer allocation, then evaluate a selected checkpoint and the current best-known candidate on the same full official-range development panel with radius-, angle-, first-reach-, and complete-hold diagnostics. Close with a positive, negative, limited, or inconclusive artifact-comparison conclusion when the paired results establish whether inner pre-reach success improved and whether outer complete-hold performance was preserved; retain unresolved causal attribution as a frontier rather than treating the factor bundle as causal.
request.goal_connection: The best measured candidate succeeds on 42/93 inner-band episodes (45.16%) but 63/67 outer-band episodes (94.03%), with 45 inner failures before any reach and no outer post-reach incomplete holds. A candidate trained with explicit 0.06-0.20 m exposure and deliberate reset escape/two-branch coverage could directly address the dominant measured gap while retaining the authoritative complete 100-step hold evaluation; improvement would increase the prospect of reaching the 98% official objective, whereas deterioration would identify a tradeoff that must be resolved before assessment.
request.question: Can an explicitly broadened official-radius training exposure with deliberate reset-escape and two-branch coverage improve the inner-radius/approach deficit while preserving the candidate's outer-radius uninterrupted-hold performance under the full official distribution?
request.rationale: Official assessment is terminal and the only measured candidate is far below 98%, so its likely fail result has little decision value compared with one bounded attempt targeted at the identified failure regime. Existing evidence supports inner approach/escape as the candidate bottleneck but does not distinguish exposure, reset sequencing, branch choice, or angle effects. The proposed inquiry changes and records those training conditions together, making the immediate scientific claim a comparison of complete artifacts. It is implementable in the PI-owned training environment without changing protected task or evaluation semantics, and its result can either improve the candidate prospect or redirect the next decision.

request.current_goal_gap: The candidate has a large full-distribution gap: 42/93 inner-band successes (45.16%) versus 63/67 outer-band successes (94.03%). Inner failures are primarily before any reach (45), with 6 after reach without a complete hold; outer failures are 4 before reach and none after reach without a complete hold. Official 98% performance is unmeasured and unmet. The next gap is to obtain a candidate with materially improved inner approach/escape success without losing the already strong outer uninterrupted-hold behavior.
request.current_synthesis: Established observations: M3 found 50 Hz control, finite compiled inertial quantities, bounded motor authority, damping-related velocity decay, repeatable nonzero responses, and a reset singularity-direction asymmetry in five deterministic postures and bounded command probes. Those probes weaken a blanket nominal torque/inertia impossibility explanation, but do not test learned target-directed behavior. T1 used PPO with 120,832 actual rounded steps, exposed training targets only to radii 0.14-0.20 m, and reached a late training proxy near 0.96-0.97; the proxy is not development performance and the terminal checkpoint is not privileged. M4 measured the archived late-plateau checkpoint on 160 full-range episodes at 65.625% success. M6 verified complete radius and angle coverage; the inner/outer contrast and failure timing show a candidate-level approach/escape deficit, while regulation after successful outer-band arrival is comparatively adequate. Angle-sector success still ranged from 48.39% to 92.11%. Correction to the inherited interpretation: inner-radius/branch coverage and reset escape are a useful first intervention target for this candidate, not an established causal diagnosis. M6 contains aggregate radius/angle and hold diagnostics but no branch or reset-sequence attribution, and T1 did not deliberately vary or balance those factors. The physical model therefore makes several consequential alternatives live: insufficient inner-radius exposure, escape sequencing from the singular reset, analytic branch selection, and angle-dependent coverage; observation sufficiency and hidden hold state remain secondary alternatives because post-reach failures were uncommon in the outer band. The proposed comparison changes the training exposure and deliberate escape/branch coverage together, so any result will establish a property of the complete compared artifacts, not the isolated causal effect of one factor. Protected task mechanics, target distribution, success semantics, and evaluation hold diagnostics will remain unchanged.
request.decision_frontier: The consequential unresolved distinction is whether a candidate trained with full official-radius exposure plus deliberate reset escape and both analytic branches improves the inner pre-reach regime while preserving outer complete-hold regulation. The discriminating evidence is a selected-checkpoint versus T1:checkpoint-115712 comparison on identical full official-range development seeds, reporting overall success, inner and outer success, failures before reach, first-reach timing, post-reach incomplete holds, interruptions, and angle sectors. A rise in inner pre-reach success with preserved outer hold performance supports this artifact direction; persistent inner failure redirects toward representation/optimization or more specific reset/branch investigation; new post-reach interruptions reopen stabilization or hidden temporal-state concerns. M3's plant characterization remains relevant only if the broadened candidate shows bounded, repeatable failures consistent with authority or singularity limits; it does not by itself justify assessment or a plant-level conclusion.
request.human_goal_connection: The immutable goal is at least 196 successes out of 200 official episodes, with every success requiring an uninterrupted 100-step hold within 1 cm. The only measured learned candidate, T1:checkpoint-115712, achieved 105/160 (65.625%) on a full-range development panel, so assessment now would be a likely terminal failure rather than evidence of readiness. Inquiry I2 is opened to develop the dominant measured inner-radius approach capability while protecting outer complete-hold behavior.
